audit_scope.scope_statement: aml_readiness_review for fintech across US, UK
evidence_missing_at_start: Enterprise AML policy approved and version controlled
Compliance governance roles and escalation paths defined
Beneficial ownership and business verification controls documented

executive_summary.system_or_business_reviewed: Real AML Case 001 payments platform specializing in wallet and cross-border payments for SMB and consumer customers in US and UK.
executive_summary.overall_readiness: The AML readiness review identified partial alignment with regulatory expectations but significant gaps remain in key controls including beneficial ownership, customer identification, and sanctions screening within the US and UK regimes.
top_issues: Insufficient evidence of effective sanctions screening (SAN-001).
Incomplete documentation for customer identification and verification (KYC-001).
Lack of comprehensive beneficial ownership controls (CDD_BO).
executive_summary.decision_summary: Critical decision points were impacted by unavailability of controls and evidence relating to key AML components, requiring immediate remediation to meet BSA/AML, UK MLR, and related regimes.
executive_summary.board_message: The AML readiness of Real AML Case 001 reveals critical vulnerabilities in governance, customer due diligence, and sanctions screening that must be addressed promptly to mitigate regulatory and operational risk exposure.

deployment_decision.decision_rationale: Deployment blocked due to missing critical/high-severity controls or insufficient confidence.

findings.title: Deficient Sanctions Screening Procedures
findings.description: No substantive evidence found to demonstrate robust sanctions screening mechanisms compliant with SAN-001 control requirements across US and UK jurisdictions.

findings.title: Inadequate Customer Identification and Verification
findings.description: Customer identification and verification controls (KYC-001) lack comprehensive documentation and verifiable operationalization, impeding effective risk management.

findings.title: Insufficient Beneficial Ownership Controls
findings.description: Controls pertaining to beneficial ownership identification (CDD_BO) are incomplete, exposing the entity to risks of unidentified or improperly assessed ownership structures.

findings.title: Governance and Policy Framework Deficiencies
findings.description: The governance framework and policy documentation (GOV-001) require enhancements to ensure alignment with regulatory regimes and audit expectations.

key_risks.description: Deficient controls and evidence gaps increase likelihood of breaches against BSA AML, UK MLR and related requirements, risking penalties and enforcement actions.
Insufficient sanctions screening and beneficial ownership verification could allow illicit actors to abuse the payments platform, leading to fraud and reputational damage.

immediate_0_30_days: Conduct comprehensive review of sanctions screening processes and implement missing controls per SAN-001.
Begin documentation and formalization of customer identification procedures compliant with KYC-001.
near_term_30_90_days: Enhance beneficial ownership identification controls in alignment with CDD_BO requirements.
Review and update governance policies to address identified gaps under GOV-001.
medium_term_90_180_days: Implement ongoing monitoring and testing of sanctions screening and KYC controls to demonstrate operational effectiveness.
Engage compliance training focused on AML regulatory regimes and control responsibilities.
strategic_180_plus_days: Establish continuous improvement processes and risk-based approaches to AML compliance embedded in organizational culture.
Implement technology solutions to support automated sanctions screening and beneficial ownership determination.

reporting_outputs.board_ready_summary: The AML readiness review revealed critical gaps in sanctions screening, customer verification, and beneficial ownership controls that expose the entity to significant regulatory and operational risks. Immediate remediation activities are essential to achieve compliance with US and UK AML obligations.
reporting_outputs.regulator_ready_summary: Review findings indicate the entity has yet to fully implement key AML controls including sanctions screening (SAN-001), customer identification and verification (KYC-001), and beneficial ownership processes (CDD_BO) in accordance with BSA AML and UK MLR requirements. Governance framework improvements are also needed. Remediation plans are in place to address these deficiencies.
reporting_outputs.client_facing_summary: Our AML readiness assessment identified areas needing improvement in sanctions screening, customer due diligence, and policies to meet US and UK regulatory standards. We recommend prioritized actions to strengthen controls and governance to ensure compliance and reduce financial crime risk.
